app.title: IRS Survival Explorer (Immune Risk Score survival explorer)
app.summary: A person loads a differential expression table and a gene set enrichment table, or uses the bundled ones, and sets significance cut-offs in a sidebar. The interface takes the significant genes that match a list of immune-gene prefixes and combines them into one risk score per patient, weighted by fold change. Because the expression results come with no outcome data, it simulates a patient cohort and splits it into high and low groups at the median. It then fits survival curves, a log-rank test and a proportional-hazards model with covariates, and checks the proportional-hazards assumption. The person can look at supporting plots of the expression, enrichment and network results, then download the simulated cohort table.

task.text: Turn differential expression and enrichment results into a composite risk score and see how it separates survival, and how sensitive that is to each cut-off.

data.text: Per-gene differential expression statistics and per-term enrichment results as tables, which are turned into a simulated patient table of time-to-event outcomes with covariates. Precomputed protein-interaction network outputs are also shown.
data.item: a gene with its fold change and adjusted p-value, rolled up into one patient's risk score with a survival time and event flag

stage.text: linking expression results to survival outcome, after differential expression and enrichment analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar cut-offs and simulation settings feed one recomputation, and its results show in a row of header metrics and in tabs: survival curves with a forest plot, a volcano plot with the selected genes, an enrichment lollipop chart, a network viewer and the cohort table. Each change in the sidebar redraws every view from the same fitted models.

field.text: survival analysis of a transcriptomic risk score in cancer bioinformatics

workflow.name: build a composite score from selected features and test how it splits outcomes

steps.here: Upload a DESeq2 results CSV and a clusterProfiler GSEA CSV in the sidebar. With no uploads, the bundled files are used. Required columns are checked on load.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Set the padj and |log2FC| cut-offs for genes and the FDR cut-off for enrichment terms. The volcano plot draws the thresholds, and a table lists the immune-prefix genes that enter the score.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Simulate a cohort from the fold-change-weighted score, using the chosen cohort size, follow-up and seed. The effect size comes from the mean negative enrichment score, and the cohort is split into High and Low at the median.

Show Kaplan-Meier curves for High and Low groups with censor marks, the log-rank statistic and median survival per group. A Cox model of score, age and stage is shown as a forest plot and a hazard-ratio table, with an adjustable penalizer.

steps.step: check that the model's assumption holds
steps.here: A Schoenfeld residual test table flags covariates whose effect changes over time.
A lollipop chart of the most negatively enriched terms, with a slider for how many terms to show, and a precomputed protein-interaction network with hub-gene and centrality tables.
Download the simulated patient table as a CSV.

distinctive: The outcome cohort is simulated from observed effect sizes, so the tool demonstrates the method and is not evidence. A fixed seed makes it reproduce a reference file.
The score's features are chosen by a gene-symbol prefix rule, with a fallback to all significant genes when nothing matches.
Changing the seed, cohort size or follow-up shows how stable the survival estimates are under resampling.
Covariates are drawn independently of survival, so their hazard ratios act as a negative control.
The proportional-hazards assumption is tested next to the model that relies on it.
